key_insight: Federated learning can potentially deliver personalised breast cancer progression prediction using multimodal data while keeping patient data local.
clinical_relevance: If validated, this approach could support privacy-preserving decision support for personalised treatment planning across hospitals.
method: Trained a federated model on multimodal breast cancer data, including clinical, tumour, biomarker, demographic, and MRI information.
Compared federated performance against a centralised model trained on pooled data.
Assessed deployment priorities including transparency, scalability, security, and fairness.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a direct comparison between federated and centralised models to judge whether privacy-preserving learning can achieve comparable predictive performance.
watch_item: Performance, fairness, and security may vary across institutions and patient subgroups, so real-world deployment needs careful validation and governance.
paper_title: Trustworthy Privacy-Preserving Multimodal Federated Learning for Personalised Breast Cancer Prediction
